title: Backstop Capability Schema v1
description: Schema for user capabilities — automated user acceptance testing as a first-class artifact. Each capability declares what a user can do, specifies behavioral scenarios (Gherkin), and provides executable verification that proves the capability works end-to-end. Stack-agnostic: works for web apps, CLIs, APIs, mobile, desktop — any user-facing feature in any tech stack.

directory_structure.description: Each capability lives in its own directory with co-located behavioral scenarios and acceptance tests.

title.description: Human-readable title describing what the user can do

status.description: Lifecycle status. verified = acceptance tests pass. broken = acceptance tests fail.

strictness.description: Enforcement level. strict = gate blocks on failure. standard = gate warns. relaxed = gate reports only (bootstrap mode).

description.description: What this capability enables the user to do

infrastructure_specs.description: Spec IDs (SPEC-NNN) that implement the infrastructure this capability depends on. These are the unit/component-level specs — capabilities verify the integration layer above them.

integration_spec.description: The spec that wires infrastructure together for this capability. The integration point where unit-tested pieces become a working feature.

feature_file.description: Path to the Gherkin .feature file relative to the capability directory

id_pattern.description: Regex pattern for scenario IDs. Each scenario must have a unique ID tag.

app_origins.description: Application URLs or endpoints to test against (web apps, APIs). Empty for CLI tools.

auth_strategy.description: How authentication is handled during acceptance tests

setup_command.description: Command to run before acceptance tests (start server, seed data, etc.)

teardown_command.description: Command to run after acceptance tests (stop server, cleanup, etc.)

performance_requirements.description: Performance targets that must be met for the capability to be considered verified

metric.description: What is being measured (e.g., feedback_latency, page_load, command_execution)

quality_gates.description: Commands that must pass for the capability to be verified. Stack-agnostic — each gate is a command + exit code check. Could be Playwright, go test, curl, a shell script, anything.

command.description: The command to run. Exit 0 = pass, non-zero = fail.

enforcement.scenario-coverage: Every scenario in the .feature file (tagged @UJ-NNN) must have a corresponding test in the acceptance test file with a matching name/ID
enforcement.scenario-uniqueness: Each @UJ-NNN tag must be unique within the .feature file
enforcement.gate-execution: All quality_gates with must_pass: true must exit 0 for the capability status to be 'verified'
enforcement.infrastructure-traceability: Every infrastructure_spec must exist as a real spec artifact
enforcement.status-integrity: Status 'verified' can only be set when all gates pass. Status 'broken' must be set when any gate fails.

verified.description: All quality gates pass, all scenarios have corresponding tests

broken.description: At least one quality gate fails or scenario coverage is incomplete
broken.trigger: any quality_gate with must_pass=true exits non-zero
